findings.source_passage: I feel funny. Fa, la! lirra, skirra! What's my juicy little pear at home doing now? Crying its eyes out?—Giving a party to the last arrived harpooneers
findings.source_locator: middle of Stubb's soliloquy, after 'I'll go to it laughing'
findings.why_it_matters: The 'juicy little pear' aside is one of Stubb's most characteristically comic, self-deflating domestic touches; it establishes his comic persona and the ironic contrast between domestic sentiment and seafaring bravado that critics note as voice-defining.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the 'What's my juicy little pear at home doing now? Crying its eyes out?—Giving a party to the last arrived harpooneers, I dare say, gay as a frigate's pennant' passage; it is short and essential to Stubb's voice.

findings.source_passage: Such a waggish leering as lurks in all your horribles! I feel funny.
findings.source_locator: after 'I'll go to it laughing', before 'Fa, la!'
findings.why_it_matters: 'Such a waggish leering as lurks in all your horribles' is a rhetorically distinctive, tonally loaded phrase that captures Stubb's philosophy of comic fatalism; its absence flattens the interpretive texture of his response to Ahab's intensity.
findings.suggested_fix: Insert the line 'Such a waggish leering as lurks in all your horribles! I feel funny.' between 'I'll go to it laughing' and the 'Fa, la!' refrain.

findings.source_passage: had had the gift, might readily have prophesied it—for when I clapped my eye upon his skull I saw it.
findings.source_locator: early in Stubb's soliloquy, after 'Be sure the old Mogul has fixed him, too'
findings.why_it_matters: The skull-reading aside carries interpretive weight about Ahab's physical marking and Stubb's preternatural sense of fate; it anticipates later symbolism around Ahab's physiognomy.
findings.suggested_fix: Consider adding a compressed version: 'I twigged it—when I clapped my eye upon his skull I saw it.' to preserve the interpretive motif.

findings.source_passage: he's my superior, he has his too, if I'm not mistaken
findings.source_locator: final line, the aside after Starbuck calls
findings.why_it_matters: The aside about Starbuck having 'his too' (i.e., his own predestinated doom) is a small but pointed ironic parenthesis that links the chapter's fatalism motif back to the Starbuck-Ahab dynamic.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the aside: '(aside) he's my superior, he has his too, if I'm not mistaken' in the closing line.

summary: No high-severity losses; two medium-severity omissions (the 'juicy little pear' passage and 'waggish leering' line) flatten Stubb's distinctive comic-fatalist voice but do not individually trigger regeneration, and two low-severity cuts thin the interpretive texture without destroying it.
